title: AKI and renal drug dosing
summary: Acute kidney injury in the ICU: KDIGO staging, a structured work-up, rhabdomyolysis, contrast-associated AKI, practical renal drug dosing, and hepatorenal and cardiorenal syndromes, with Indian causes (tropical infections, snakebite, indigenous medicines).

topics.title: KDIGO definition and staging
topics.summary: Define and stage AKI with creatinine and urine output, and recognise who needs urgent nephrology/ICU input.

definition.text: AKI (KDIGO 2012) = creatinine rise ≥ 0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, OR rise to ≥ 1.5x baseline within the prior 7 days, OR urine output < 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 h.

steps.title: Find a baseline creatinine
steps.detail: Lowest value in the last 3 months (or up to 1 year). If unknown, use the lowest value during admission; avoid back-calculating from eGFR in Indian patients with low muscle mass.

steps.title: Stage by the worse of creatinine or urine output
steps.detail: Stage 1: 1.5-1.9x baseline or ≥ 0.3 mg/dL rise; UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6-12 h. Stage 2: 2.0-2.9x; UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h ≥ 12 h. Stage 3: ≥ 3x or creatinine ≥ 4.0 mg/dL or RRT started; UO < 0.3 mL/kg/h ≥ 24 h or anuria ≥ 12 h.

steps.title: Measure urine output hourly
steps.detail: Urinary catheter in critically ill/oliguric patients; use actual body weight (consider ideal weight in obesity).

steps.title: Apply the KDIGO bundle at any stage
steps.detail: Stop nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast if avoidable), review drug doses, ensure volume status and perfusion pressure (MAP ≥ 65), monitor creatinine and UO, avoid hyperglycaemia, consider alternatives to radiocontrast.

steps.title: Escalate stage 2-3
steps.detail: Nephrology/ICU review, search for cause (see AKI work-up), assess RRT needs (hyperkalaemia, acidosis, overload, uraemic complications).

tables.title: KDIGO AKI staging
rows: 1.5-1.9x baseline OR ≥ 0.3 mg/dL rise in 48 h
≥ 3x baseline OR ≥ 4.0 mg/dL OR RRT initiated
< 0.3 mL/kg/h for ≥ 24 h OR anuria ≥ 12 h

redFlags.text: AKI with K ≥ 6.5 mmol/L, pH < 7.15, pulmonary oedema not responding to diuretics, or uraemic encephalopathy/pericarditis: emergency RRT assessment.

pitfalls.text: Creatinine lags 24-48 h behind injury, and fluid overload dilutes it; urine output falls earlier.
Using eGFR equations in unstable AKI: they assume steady state.

pearls.text: A small creatinine rise (0.3 mg/dL) independently predicts mortality; treat it seriously.

nodes.text: Creatinine rise or low urine output
Monitor creatinine and UO; avoid nephrotoxins
Stage (worst of creatinine or UO); start KDIGO bundle
AKI work-up: volume, obstruction (USG), urine, drugs, sepsis
Nephrology/ICU review; daily RRT need assessment
Treat cause, daily review, repeat creatinine in 24 h

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: AKI reflects an abrupt fall in GFR from haemodynamic (pre-renal), intrinsic (ATN, interstitial nephritis, glomerulonephritis, vascular) or post-renal causes. In ICU, sepsis-associated AKI is the commonest and involves inflammation and microvascular dysfunction rather than simple hypoperfusion.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- KDIGO 2012 unified RIFLE and AKIN criteria; even stage 1 AKI is associated with increased mortality [KDIGO 2012].
- KDIGO care bundles in high-risk patients (PrevAKI trials) reduced AKI after cardiac surgery.
consultantNotes.controversies:
- Biomarkers (NGAL, TIMP-2·IGFBP7) for early detection are not widely used in India due to cost.
- Urine output criterion with actual vs ideal body weight in obesity.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Community-acquired AKI in India is often due to tropical infections (leptospirosis, malaria, scrub typhus, dengue), snakebite (Russell's viper), diarrhoeal illness, and nephrotoxic indigenous medicines; it affects younger patients.
- Creatinine is reported in mg/dL in India (1 mg/dL = 88.4 µmol/L).

topics.title: AKI work-up
topics.summary: A structured bedside approach to the cause: pre-renal, intrinsic, post-renal, with urine tests, ultrasound and the furosemide stress test.

definition.text: Look for the cause of every AKI: volume/perfusion, sepsis, nephrotoxins, obstruction, and intrinsic renal disease (glomerulonephritis, interstitial nephritis, vascular). Most ICU AKI is multifactorial.

steps.title: History and drug chart
steps.detail: Hypotension, sepsis, vomiting/diarrhoea, contrast, NSAIDs, ACEi/ARB, diuretics, aminoglycosides, vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam, colistin, amphotericin, herbal/indigenous medicines, snakebite, rhabdomyolysis risk.

steps.title: Assess volume and perfusion
steps.detail: MAP, CRT, lactate, JVP/CVP, lung B-lines, IVC, fluid balance; venous congestion (high CVP) also reduces GFR.

steps.title: Exclude obstruction
steps.detail: Bladder scan / catheter flush; renal ultrasound for hydronephrosis, kidney size (small = CKD), stones.

steps.title: Urine tests
steps.detail: Dipstick (blood/protein), microscopy (muddy brown casts = ATN; RBC casts = GN; WBC casts/eosinophils = AIN), urine Na/FeNa (< 1% suggests pre-renal if not on diuretics), FeUrea < 35% if on diuretics, urine protein:creatinine.

steps.title: Bloods
steps.detail: Creatinine, urea, K, bicarbonate/ABG, Ca, PO4, CK (rhabdo), LDH and smear (haemolysis, TMA), platelets, LFT, cultures. Serology if GN suspected: ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, C3/C4, hepatitis B/C, HIV.

steps.title: Furosemide stress test (optional)
steps.detail: Euvolaemic, stage 1-2 AKI: furosemide 1 mg/kg IV (1.5 mg/kg if exposed); urine < 200 mL in 2 h predicts progression to stage 3/RRT.

steps.title: Refer for biopsy/nephrology
steps.detail: Active sediment, nephrotic-range proteinuria, unexplained AKI, suspected vasculitis/TMA or AIN.

doseCards.dose: 1 mg/kg (1.5 mg/kg if on loop diuretics)
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg diuretic-naive: 70 mg IV; replace urine output mL-for-mL with crystalloid if needed; < 200 mL in 2 h = high risk

tables.title: Causes of AKI in Indian ICUs
rows: Sepsis, hypovolaemia (diarrhoea, vomiting, bleeding), cardiorenal, hepatorenal, ACEi/NSAIDs
Ischaemic/septic ATN, contrast, aminoglycosides, colistin, rhabdomyolysis, haemolysis (G6PD, malaria), snakebite
Post-infectious GN, lupus, vasculitis, HUS/TTP, malignant hypertension
BPH, stones, cervical/prostate cancer, blocked catheter

redFlags.text: AKI with haemoptysis (pulmonary-renal syndrome), active urine sediment or rapidly rising creatinine: urgent nephrology, consider vasculitis/anti-GBM.
AKI + thrombocytopenia + haemolysis (schistocytes, high LDH): think TMA (HUS/TTP), malaria, snakebite, DIC.

pitfalls.text: Interpreting FeNa after diuretics; use FeUrea instead.
Giving more fluid to every oliguric patient: fluid overload worsens AKI outcome.

pearls.text: Always flush or replace the urinary catheter before calling it anuria.

nodes.text: Active sediment (RBC casts, proteinuria) or systemic features?
Probable ATN/septic AKI: supportive care, monitor, RRT if needed

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Pre-renal states cause avid sodium and water retention (low urine Na, FeNa < 1%), which reverses quickly with restored perfusion. Prolonged insult leads to tubular injury with loss of concentrating ability (urine Na > 40, FeNa > 2%, muddy brown casts).
consultantNotes.evidence:
- Chawla 2013: furosemide stress test urine < 200 mL in 2 h had AUC 0.87 for progression to stage 3 [Chawla 2013].
- KDIGO 2012 recommends evaluating cause in all AKI and avoiding diuretics to prevent or treat AKI except for fluid overload [KDIGO 2012].
consultantNotes.controversies: - FeNa is unreliable in sepsis, contrast nephropathy and CKD.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Ask specifically about indigenous medicines (some contain heavy metals or aristolochic acid), hair dye (paraphenylenediamine) ingestion, and snakebite.
- Leptospirosis AKI is typically non-oliguric with hypokalaemia; Russell's viper AKI often needs RRT.

topics.title: Rhabdomyolysis
topics.summary: Recognise rhabdomyolysis, give early aggressive fluids, manage hyperkalaemia and compartment syndrome, and know when to start RRT.

definition.text: Rhabdomyolysis = skeletal muscle breakdown releasing myoglobin, K, phosphate and urate; CK typically > 5x upper limit (often > 5,000-10,000 U/L). AKI risk rises with CK > 15,000-20,000 U/L, dehydration, acidosis and sepsis.

steps.title: Suspect
steps.detail: Crush injury, prolonged immobilisation (stroke, intoxication), seizures, heat stroke, extreme exertion, electrical injury, snakebite (sea snake, Russell's viper), drugs (statins, colchicine), hypokalaemia/hypophosphataemia, infections (leptospirosis, dengue, influenza).

steps.title: Confirm and grade
steps.detail: CK (peaks 24-72 h), dark urine with dipstick positive for blood but no RBCs on microscopy, K, Ca (low), PO4 (high), urate, creatinine, ABG, ECG.

steps.title: Fluids early
steps.detail: Start isotonic crystalloid early (ideally before extrication in crush): 1-2 L/h initially if not overloaded, then titrate to urine output 200-300 mL/h; continue until CK < 5,000 U/L and urine clears.

steps.title: Treat hyperkalaemia
steps.detail: ECG; calcium gluconate for ECG changes, insulin-dextrose, salbutamol; avoid calcium for asymptomatic hypocalcaemia (Ca deposits in muscle, rebound hypercalcaemia later).

steps.title: Watch compartments
steps.detail: Pain on passive stretch, tense limb, rising CK: measure compartment pressure (> 30 mmHg or delta pressure < 30 mmHg) → fasciotomy.

steps.title: Bicarbonate and mannitol: not routine
steps.detail: No proven benefit; bicarbonate only for severe acidosis; mannitol not recommended.

steps.title: RRT when indicated
steps.detail: Refractory hyperkalaemia, acidosis, overload or oliguric AKI. Conventional dialysis does not remove myoglobin significantly; RRT treats complications.

doseCards.dose: 1-2 L/h initially, then titrate to UO 200-300 mL/h
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg crush victim: 1 L/h for first 2 h, then adjust to keep 200-300 mL/h; reassess lungs 2-hourly
doseCards.notes: Reduce if oliguric despite fluids (established AKI) or overloaded.

redFlags.text: K > 6.5 mmol/L or ECG changes in rhabdomyolysis can rise rapidly: treat and arrange RRT early.
Oliguria despite adequate fluid resuscitation = established AKI: stop pushing fluids, plan RRT.

pitfalls.text: Correcting early hypocalcaemia with calcium in asymptomatic patients.
Missing compartment syndrome in a sedated patient.

pearls.text: Dipstick positive for blood but no RBCs on microscopy = myoglobin or haemoglobin.

nodes.text: CK, K, Ca, PO4, creatinine, ABG, ECG, urine dipstick
Continue until CK < 5,000 and urine clear; daily CK, creatinine

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Myoglobin is filtered and, in acidic concentrated urine, precipitates with Tamm-Horsfall protein forming obstructive casts; its haem iron causes oxidative tubular injury, and it scavenges nitric oxide causing renal vasoconstriction. Volume sequestration in injured muscle adds hypovolaemia.
consultantNotes.evidence: - Bosch 2009 review: early aggressive volume expansion is the mainstay; bicarbonate and mannitol lack evidence [Bosch 2009].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Choice of fluid (saline vs balanced): no clear difference; balanced may cause less hyperchloraemic acidosis.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Common Indian causes: heat stroke in labourers, snakebite, leptospirosis, exertion (army training, marathons), crush in building collapses and earthquakes, OP poisoning-related seizures.

quiz.explanation: High urine flow reduces cast formation.

topics.title: Contrast-associated AKI
topics.summary: Assess risk, avoid unnecessary withholding of contrast, and use isotonic fluids for high-risk patients.

definition.text: Contrast-associated AKI (CA-AKI) = AKI within 48-72 h after contrast; contrast-induced AKI (CI-AKI) implies causation. True risk with modern IV contrast is much lower than previously thought, mainly in eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m².

steps.title: Do not delay life-saving imaging
steps.detail: In emergencies (stroke, PE, trauma, dissection, sepsis source) give contrast regardless of creatinine.

steps.title: Assess risk
steps.detail: eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² (non-dialysis) or AKI = high risk. eGFR 30-44: intermediate (individual decision). eGFR ≥ 45: very low risk.

steps.title: Prophylaxis for high risk
steps.detail: Isotonic crystalloid if not contraindicated (heart failure, overload): e.g. 1 mL/kg/h for 6-12 h before and after (or 3 mL/kg over 1 h before and 1 mL/kg/h for 6 h after for urgent procedures).

steps.title: Use lowest dose of iso- or low-osmolar contrast
steps.detail: Avoid repeated studies within 48-72 h if possible.

steps.title: No N-acetylcysteine or bicarbonate
steps.detail: PRESERVE (2018): neither IV bicarbonate nor oral NAC reduced death, dialysis or persistent kidney decline.

steps.title: Metformin and dialysis
steps.detail: Hold metformin if eGFR < 30 or AKI (lactic acidosis risk). Dialysis patients do not need urgent post-contrast dialysis unless volume overloaded.

steps.title: Check creatinine at 48-72 h
steps.detail: In high-risk patients.

doseCards.dose: 1 mL/kg/h for 6-12 h before and after contrast
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg, eGFR 25: 70 mL/h from 6 h before to 6-12 h after CT
doseCards.notes: Not in heart failure or overload.

redFlags.text: Withholding contrast CT from a patient with suspected PE, stroke or abdominal sepsis because of 'high creatinine' is more dangerous than CA-AKI.

pitfalls.text: Blaming contrast for AKI caused by sepsis, hypotension or nephrotoxins given at the same time.

pearls.text: Most creatinine rises after CT in ICU patients are coincidental; propensity-matched studies show similar AKI rates with and without contrast at eGFR ≥ 30.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Iodinated contrast causes renal medullary vasoconstriction and direct tubular toxicity; risk is greatest with high doses, intra-arterial injection (first-pass renal exposure), volume depletion and severe CKD.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ACR-NKF 2020 consensus: prophylaxis indicated for eGFR < 30 not on dialysis and AKI; consider for 30-44 with other risk factors [Davenport 2020].
- PRESERVE (5,177 patients undergoing angiography): no benefit of bicarbonate vs saline or NAC vs placebo [Weisbord 2018].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Whether CI-AKI after IV contrast exists at all in eGFR ≥ 30 is debated.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Iso-osmolar contrast (iodixanol) is costlier; low-osmolar agents (iohexol, iopamidol) are standard in India.
- Many Indian centres still give NAC by habit; it is not harmful but not effective.

quiz.stem: Patient with suspected PE has creatinine 2.4 mg/dL. Best action:
options: Proceed with CTPA; IV fluids if not overloaded
No benefit of either bicarbonate or NAC

topics.title: Drug dosing in AKI
topics.summary: Estimate kidney function correctly in unstable AKI and adjust common ICU drugs, with loading doses unchanged.

definition.text: In unstable AKI, creatinine-based equations overestimate GFR when creatinine is rising and underestimate it during recovery. Give full loading doses (volume of distribution is unchanged or increased), then adjust maintenance doses and use therapeutic drug monitoring where available.

steps.title: Estimate clearance sensibly
steps.detail: Use Cockcroft-Gault for drug dosing (most labels); in unstable AKI assume GFR < 10-25 mL/min if creatinine rising rapidly or anuric. Measured 4-6 h urinary creatinine clearance is better in ICU.

steps.title: Never reduce the loading dose
steps.detail: Antibiotics, antiepileptics, digoxin load: full dose. Underdosing antibiotics in early sepsis is a bigger risk than toxicity.

steps.title: Adjust maintenance
steps.detail: Extend interval (aminoglycosides, vancomycin) or reduce dose (beta-lactams per CrCl). Reassess daily as AKI evolves; augment as kidneys recover.

steps.title: Use TDM
steps.detail: Vancomycin trough or AUC (target AUC 400-600 mg.h/L), aminoglycoside levels, (beta-lactam TDM where available).

steps.title: Avoid or replace nephrotoxins
steps.detail: NSAIDs, aminoglycosides (unless essential), IV contrast where possible, amphotericin deoxycholate (use liposomal), colistin with TDM/limit duration. Hold ACEi/ARB, metformin, SGLT2i during AKI.

steps.title: Watch accumulating drugs
steps.detail: Morphine (active metabolites → use fentanyl), midazolam (active metabolite), pethidine (avoid), enoxaparin (CrCl < 30: 1 mg/kg once daily or UFH), gabapentin, pregabalin, digoxin, LMWH, meropenem/cefepime (neurotoxicity), sotalol.

tables.title: Common ICU drugs: adjustment in AKI (CrCl < 30 mL/min, not on RRT)
rows: CrCl 30-60: 2 g q12h; 11-29: 2 g q24h; risk of neurotoxicity
Same load; maintenance by levels (often q24-48h)
Extend interval by levels (q36-48h) or avoid
Same load; maintenance reduced per CrCl
Load unchanged; then 50% maintenance if CrCl < 50
tables.caption: Adapted from product labels and standard references; always cross-check with a current drug reference or ICU pharmacist.

redFlags.text: New confusion, myoclonus or seizures on cefepime, meropenem, or high-dose penicillins in AKI: suspect drug neurotoxicity.

pitfalls.text: Halving the first dose of antibiotics in septic AKI.
Forgetting to increase doses again when kidney function recovers or augmented renal clearance develops.

pearls.text: Use the calculator for Cockcroft-Gault, but remember it overestimates GFR in elderly, cachectic Indian patients with low muscle mass.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: AKI reduces renal elimination but often coincides with increased volume of distribution (capillary leak, fluid resuscitation), hypoalbuminaemia (more free drug) and altered hepatic metabolism. Net effect: full loads, careful maintenance, frequent reassessment.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- KDIGO 2012 recommends drug dose adjustment in AKI and TDM for aminoglycosides and vancomycin [KDIGO 2012].
- 2020 ASHP/IDSA vancomycin guideline recommends AUC-guided dosing (400-600 mg.h/L).
consultantNotes.controversies: - Optimal estimation of GFR in non-steady state (kinetic eGFR equations).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Colistin and aminoglycosides are frequently needed for CRE in Indian ICUs; nephrotoxicity is common: limit duration, ensure hydration and monitor creatinine daily.
- Vancomycin level testing is not available in all hospitals; use conservative dosing and creatinine monitoring.

topics.title: Hepatorenal and cardiorenal syndromes
topics.summary: Diagnose HRS-AKI by ICA-ADQI 2024 criteria and treat with terlipressin and albumin; manage cardiorenal syndrome by decongestion.

definition.text: HRS-AKI = AKI in cirrhosis with ascites, no response after 48 h of diuretic withdrawal and albumin 1 g/kg, no shock, no current nephrotoxins, no signs of structural kidney injury. Cardiorenal syndrome = bidirectional heart-kidney dysfunction; type 1 = acute heart failure causing AKI, often driven by venous congestion.

steps.title: Cirrhosis with AKI: first steps
steps.detail: Stop diuretics, NSAIDs, beta-blockers if hypotensive, nephrotoxins; treat infection (SBP: diagnostic tap), bleeding, hypovolaemia (albumin 1 g/kg/day, max 100 g, for 2 days).

steps.title: Diagnose HRS-AKI
steps.detail: If AKI persists (stage ≥ 1B or progressing) without shock and urine sediment is bland (protein < 500 mg/day, < 50 RBC/hpf, normal ultrasound): HRS-AKI.

steps.title: Treat HRS-AKI
steps.detail: Terlipressin (bolus 0.5-1 mg q4-6h or infusion 2 mg/day, up-titrate to max 12 mg/day) + albumin 20-40 g/day. Noradrenaline infusion is an alternative in ICU (central line). Midodrine + octreotide is less effective.

steps.title: Monitor for harm
steps.detail: Daily SpO2, chest exam, fluid status: terlipressin + albumin can cause pulmonary oedema and respiratory failure. Stop if SpO2 < 90%; avoid in ACLF grade 3 or creatinine ≥ 5 mg/dL.

steps.title: Response and transplant
steps.detail: Response = creatinine fall to < 0.3 mg/dL above baseline. Refer all HRS for liver transplant assessment; RRT as bridge if transplant candidate.

steps.title: Cardiorenal: decongest
steps.detail: Loop diuretic IV at 1-2.5x oral dose; check spot urine Na at 2 h (< 50-70 mmol/L = inadequate) and UO at 6 h (< 100-150 mL/h): double dose, add thiazide/acetazolamide. A modest creatinine rise during effective decongestion is acceptable.

steps.title: Refractory cardiorenal
steps.detail: Inotrope if low output; ultrafiltration/RRT for diuretic-resistant congestion.

doseCards.dose: 0.5-1 mg q4-6h, or 2 mg/24 h infusion; max 12 mg/day
doseCards.dilution: 2 mg in 50 mL NS over 24 h = ~2 mL/h
doseCards.workedExample: Start 2 mg/24 h infusion; creatinine fall < 25% at 48 h → increase to 4 mg/24 h
doseCards.notes: Infusion has fewer ischaemic side effects than boluses.

doseCards.dose: Day 1-2: 1 g/kg/day (max 100 g); with terlipressin 20-40 g/day
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 70 g = 350 mL of 20% albumin on day 1

doseCards.dose: 1-2.5x total daily oral dose as bolus; repeat/double at 6 h if poor response
doseCards.workedExample: On oral furosemide 40 mg BD (80 mg/day): give 80-200 mg IV; urine Na at 2 h < 50 mmol/L → double dose

redFlags.text: New hypoxaemia or crackles on terlipressin + albumin: stop albumin, consider stopping terlipressin, diurese.
AKI in cirrhosis with fever or abdominal pain: diagnostic paracentesis for SBP immediately.

pitfalls.text: Continuing diuretics and lactulose-induced diarrhoea while creatinine rises in cirrhosis.
Stopping diuretics in cardiorenal syndrome because creatinine rises while the patient is still congested.

pearls.text: Creatinine overestimates GFR in cirrhosis (low muscle mass); a 'normal' creatinine of 1.0 mg/dL may be significant kidney dysfunction.

nodes.text: Stop diuretics/nephrotoxins; treat infection, bleeding; tap ascites (SBP)
Albumin 1 g/kg/day × 2 days if no overload
Pre-renal AKI resolved; cautious diuretic reintroduction
Shock or structural kidney injury (proteinuria, haematuria, abnormal USG)?
HRS-AKI: terlipressin + albumin 20-40 g/day (or noradrenaline in ICU)
Monitor SpO2/fluids; transplant referral; RRT as bridge

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: In cirrhosis, splanchnic vasodilation reduces effective arterial volume, activating RAAS, sympathetic system and vasopressin, causing intense renal vasoconstriction (HRS). Systemic inflammation from infection is a frequent trigger. In cardiorenal syndrome, raised venous pressure transmitted to the kidney (renal congestion) reduces GFR more than low forward flow.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- CONFIRM (300 patients): terlipressin + albumin increased HRS reversal (32% vs 17%) but caused more respiratory failure deaths [Wong 2021].
- ICA-ADQI 2024 consensus updated definitions of AKI and HRS-AKI in cirrhosis [Nadim 2024].
- HFA 2019 position statement: natriuresis-guided diuretic titration in congestion [Mullens 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies:
- Terlipressin infusion vs bolus; noradrenaline vs terlipressin in ICU (similar efficacy in small trials, including Indian RCTs).
- Acceptable creatinine rise during decongestion ('permissive worsening renal function').
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Terlipressin is affordable and widely used in India; many Indian RCTs (e.g. from ILBS Delhi) compared terlipressin and noradrenaline in HRS.
- Alcohol-related and hepatitis B/C cirrhosis predominate; consider ACLF triggers (alcoholic hepatitis, hepatitis E/A superinfection).

drugs.name: Furosemide
drugs.indications: Fluid overload in AKI; furosemide stress test; cardiorenal congestion
drugs.adultDose: Stress test: 1 mg/kg IV (1.5 mg/kg if already on loop diuretics). Congestion: IV dose = 1-2.5x the total daily oral dose (start 20-40 mg IV if diuretic-naive), repeat/double at 6 h if natriuresis inadequate; infusion 5-20 mg/h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 20 mg/2 mL ampoules; infusion 100 mg in 50 mL NS (2 mg/mL) or undiluted 10 mg/mL.
drugs.renalHepatic: Higher doses needed in AKI/CKD; ototoxicity with rapid high-dose bolus (> 4 mg/min).
drugs.cautions: Do not use to 'treat' oliguric AKI without fluid overload (KDIGO).
drugs.monitoring: Urine output at 2 and 6 h, spot urine sodium (> 50-70 mmol/L at 2 h = adequate response), K, Mg, creatinine.

drugs.name: Crystalloid (0.9% saline or balanced)
drugs.indications: Rhabdomyolysis; prevention of contrast AKI in high-risk patients
drugs.adultDose: Rhabdomyolysis: 1-2 L/h initially (if not overloaded), then titrate to urine output 200-300 mL/h until CK < 5,000 U/L and urine clear. Contrast prophylaxis (high risk, not overloaded): 1 mL/kg/h for 6-12 h before and after.
drugs.preparationIndia: 500 mL/1 L bags; RL also acceptable.
drugs.cautions: Stop if oliguric/anuric with overload; RRT instead.

drugs.name: Terlipressin
drugs.adultDose: HRS-AKI: 0.5-1 mg IV every 4-6 h, or continuous infusion 2 mg/24 h (fewer side effects); if creatinine falls < 25% after 48-72 h, increase stepwise to max 12 mg/day. Continue until creatinine < 1.5 mg/dL or 14 days.
drugs.preparationIndia: 1 mg vials (Indian generics widely available); infusion 2 mg in 50 mL NS over 24 h.
drugs.cautions: Avoid if SpO2 < 90%, volume overload, ischaemic heart/peripheral vascular disease, ACLF grade 3, or creatinine ≥ 5 mg/dL. Watch for respiratory failure (CONFIRM), abdominal pain, digital ischaemia, hyponatraemia.
drugs.monitoring: SpO2 and fluid status daily, creatinine, ECG.

drugs.name: Human albumin 20%
drugs.indications: HRS-AKI diagnosis and treatment; large-volume paracentesis; SBP
drugs.adultDose: AKI in cirrhosis (diagnostic challenge): 1 g/kg (max 100 g) on day 1 after stopping diuretics. HRS-AKI with terlipressin: 20-40 g/day.
drugs.cautions: Pulmonary oedema: reduce/stop if overload (CONFIRM deaths from respiratory failure).
drugs.verify: Cost is substantial for Indian families; confirm institutional dosing.
